verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Mechanical Properties of Fluids, Very Short Answer Question 7 (printed p.105). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK INCONSISTENCY: the source book's own statement of Bernoulli's principle says the total energy is constant "per unit volume", but the formula it prints in the same block, P/ρ + ½v² + gh = constant, is energy per unit mass. This answer follows the book's own formula and states the principle consistently as per unit mass, giving P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant as the equivalent per-unit-volume form. Physics hand-checked: for the steady flow of a non-viscous, incompressible fluid along a streamline, P/ρ + ½v² + gh = constant is Bernoulli's equation per unit mass — each term has units of J/kg; multiplying through by ρ gives P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant, the same relation per unit volume, with units of J/m³.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Say the sum is per unit mass, not per unit volume.
steps.why: Each term in P/ρ + ½v² + gh is an energy per unit mass — P/ρ is the pressure energy of one kilogram — so the statement must say per unit mass to match it.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two forms — saying "per unit mass" but then writing P + ½ρv² + ρgh, or saying "per unit volume" but writing P/ρ + ½v² + gh. The words and the formula must be the same form.
Leaving out non-viscous or incompressible, without which the statement does not hold.
